title: Local module isomorphisms form a sheaf
statement: Let (C,J) be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], R a ring sheaf, and M,N R-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The assignment U to the actual isomorphisms M|U ≅ N|U on C/U [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], with restriction given by overMap conjugated by the canonical overFunctorMap identifications, is a sheaf of sets.

source.place: Tag 093T, proof of (2), description of Isom as mutually inverse pairs of Hom sections.

proof.text: Construct restriction by the canonical relocalization functor and its identifications. For identity and composition, apply Iso.ext and componentwise extensionality. The corresponding identities for additive presheafHom restrictions give both functor laws. Taking hom and inv gives natural transformations to the local Hom presheaves.

For a compatible isomorphism family on a covering sieve, glue its hom family in H(M,N) and its inverse family in H(N,M). Composition and identities commute with restrictions. Separatedness of H(M,M) and H(N,N) therefore gives the two inverse identities. These glued morphisms define an actual isomorphism. Its restrictions have the prescribed hom maps and hence are the given isomorphisms. Any two gluings have equal hom maps by separatedness of H(M,N), so are equal.
